provenance.instrument: Ellwood City Borough Zoning Ordinance (Part Twelve, Title Six, Chapters 1260 to 1274, Ord. 2210 of 4-21-1997, as amended), with Chapter 1482 Flood Hazards (Ord. 2470 of 9-19-2011), as published by American Legal Publishing
provenance.status_detail: American Legal code library 'Ellwood City, PA', 'Ellwood City (Beaver/Lawrence Co)', 2025 S-27, borough office at 525 Lawrence Avenue. The borough lies mostly in Lawrence County with a small part in Beaver County. Every district's uses and figures are web text in 1266.04, with no PDF tables. The code shows zoning amendments up to Ord. 2621 of 5-20-2024 (1264.05), with Ord. 2547 of 6-18-2018 and Ord. 2563 of 5-20-2019 in 1266 and Ord. 2568 of 11-18-2019 in 1260. A 2018 council report on a downtown zoning change matches Ord. 2547, which the code shows
provenance.code_current_through_note: American Legal shows 'Local legislation current through September 15, 2025' (2025 S-27)
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit use. A search of the whole code for in-law, accessory, apartment, ECHO, granny, cottage, guesthouse, tenant, quarters, conversion, two-family and second dwelling found only the two-family and multi-family listings, the nonconforming conversion rule (1268.05), parking and building code text. The zoning definitions (1260.08) do not define family, dwelling unit, accessory use or lot coverage, so those words 'carry their customary meanings'

'Any use not expressly listed for a district is prohibited in that district', and 'Uses which are normally accessory to the declared permitted uses are also permitted' (1266.04). R-1 (A Residential) permits single-family detached dwellings and lists two-family dwellings as a special exception. R-2 (B Residential) permits single-family and two-family dwellings, and lists multi-family dwellings and individual mobile homes as special exceptions (1266.04 Table A). C-1 and C-2 list multifamily dwellings as conditional uses, on floors above the ground floor (1272.23). C-3 overlays: residential uses on the second floor or above by right in CC, multi-family dwellings by conditional use in GW and IP, apartments (three or more units) and townhouses by right and duplexes and single-family dwellings by conditional use in GN, single-family dwellings by right in IP. HM-1 and I list no dwelling. A multi-family dwelling is 'A building and lot are occupied by more than one family' (1260.08(45)), so a building with two units is one

Lot figures (1266.04): R-1 lot area 5,000 sq ft per family, building cover ('lot coverage') 40%, width 50 ft, front yard 20 ft, rear yard 30 ft, height 35 ft. R-2 lot area 4,000 sq ft per family, cover 45%, width 60 ft, front 20 ft, rear 30 ft, height 45 ft. The text above Table B gives a flat 'Minimum lot area 5,000 sq. ft.' in R-1 and 4,000 sq ft in R-2, not per family. Table 1266.04(B) gives side yards of 10 ft and 24 ft for both sides, while the text above it gives a total of 15 ft with 5 ft on one side on a lot 50 ft wide or more, down to 7 ft with 4 ft on one side on an R-2 lot just over 30 ft wide. Table B also lists 'Minimum Number of Stories' of 2 1/2 in R-1 and 4 in R-2, which reads like a story limit but is labeled a minimum, so it is not used. Where a house on one adjacent lot has a front yard deeper or shallower than 20 ft, the front yard is the average of that house's front yard and the district's 20 ft. With houses on both adjacent lots it is the average of their two front yards (1272.02(e)). A lot on two or more streets needs the front yard on every street (1272.02(a))

Accessory buildings 'shall conform to side yard requirements and shall be no less than five feet from any rear lot line' (1272.02(f)). No structure, attached or not, may project into a minimum front, side or rear yard (1272.02(b)). The code sets no size or height for an accessory building apart from the district height. Table A lists 'Accessory uses' as a conditional use in R-1, R-2, C-1 and C-2, while 1266.04 says accessory uses are also permitted, and C-2 lists them as permitted too. So an accessory building in R-1, R-2 or C-1 may need a conditional use from Borough Council. Ask the zoning officer

Parking: 'Dwellings 2 for each family or dwelling unit, including space in a garage', each space at least 180 sq ft, on the same lot as the principal use (1270.03(a), (b), (c)). Parking is due whenever a new use is established or an existing one is enlarged (1270.01), so a house turned into two units needs it. The Zoning Hearing Board may let the spaces be up to 100 ft from the lot, in the same district, where parking on the lot is impractical (1270.03(c)). A lot with no alley or access easement needs an access drive at least 10 ft wide (1270.03(a)). One- and two-family dwellings need not pave (1270.03(f)). No off-street parking is required in C-2 (1270.03(b) note)

Floodplain, Chapter 1482 (Ord. 2470 of 9-19-2011, FIRM of 1-18-2012): in the floodway any encroachment that raises flood heights is prohibited, and no new construction or development is allowed without a DEP permit (1482.18(b)(1)). In the flood fringe and the general floodplain no new construction or development may be within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of a watercourse without a DEP permit (1482.18(b)(2)B, (3)B). In a flood fringe with no designated floodway no new development may raise the base flood elevation by more than one foot with all past and projected development (1482.18(b)(2)C). New construction or a substantial improvement of a residential structure has its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft, and enclosed space below the lowest floor is prohibited (1482.03(y), 1482.22). New construction is a structure begun on or after June 1, 1982, with its later improvements (1482.03(u)). Manufactured homes and any addition to one are prohibited in the floodplain unless a variance is granted, and then they must be on a permanent foundation, elevated 1 1/2 ft above the base flood elevation and anchored (1482.25). No variance may raise the base flood elevation in a floodway, or by more than one foot in the flood fringe (1482.33(b)), and all structures must be built to resist the 100-year flood (1482.33(d)). Any construction or development anywhere in the borough needs a building permit from the Floodplain Administrator, the Zoning Officer (1482.07). The chapter has no rule on habitation of accessory structures. The Zoning Hearing Board hears floodplain variances: 1264.02(a)(3) gives it variances 'of flood plain or flood hazard ordinances', and 1482.33(b) has the Borough consider them by the procedures of 1482.17, which sends appeals to the Board

Nonconforming uses: a nonconforming building or structure may be converted into residential uses by special exception, with the district's yards and area, at least 900 sq ft of habitable living area in each unit, one bathroom and three habitable rooms (1268.05). Two units need at least 1,800 sq ft of habitable area in all. A house is a nonconforming use in C-1, C-2 and the C-3 CC and GW overlays, whose lists name no single-family dwelling. Whether converting a house that is already residential is a conversion into residential uses is not settled. A nonconforming use may not be extended or changed except to a conforming use (1268.01(b)). An extension is a special exception only if it is attached to the main structure, stays within the district's yards and height, serves the use that existed in 1997 and costs at most 80% of the building's fair market value then, and it is not permissible if any condition fails (1268.08). Repair and reconstruction may not exceed the fair replacement value (1268.04), and restoration after damage is capped at 60% and must start within six months (1268.10)
Lots of record that existed on 4-21-1997 in separate ownership may be used for a permitted use though smaller than the minimum (1272.01(a)). Adjacent small lots may be combined (1272.01(b))

Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board grants them on the five findings of MPC 910.2 (1264.03(h)). No bar on a use variance was found. The code has no steep slope, riparian or wetland rules in the zoning chapter

1272.35 lets 'A land use not expressly delineated as a permitted use, conditional use, or special exception' be a conditional use where its impacts are no greater than a listed use. Its words reach every district, while 1266.04 says 'Any use not expressly listed for a district is prohibited in that district'. This file reads 1272.35 as open only in C-3, whose lists name compatible uses not otherwise listed. Whether it reaches R-1 and R-2 is not settled, so ask the zoning officer. I has its own conditional use for uses similar to its permitted industrial uses (Table A, I 3), which is not read as a path for a dwelling

A zoning certificate from the Zoning Officer is needed before an altered or enlarged structure is occupied and before a structure's use changes, such as a house to a two-family dwelling. It expires after six months if not used (1262.03). A building permit is needed for additions and accessory structures (1262.04)

Land development: 1252.03 asks a land development application for 'residential buildings with two or more single-family units'. The state planning code says converting an existing single-family house into not more than three units is not a land development unless they are condominiums (MPC 503(1.1)), so a conversion likely needs none. A new two-family building may need one

Individual mobile homes may be a special exception in R-2 under the borough's Mobile Home Specifications (1272.07(a)). No one may live in a basement or foundation before the whole structure is done (1272.04). A home occupation stays in the house and uses at most 30% of its floor area (1272.12(b)). A rented unit falls under the borough's registration of leased properties (1046.09)

Read: 1260 (all), 1262 (all), 1264 (all), 1266 (all), 1268 (all), 1270 (all), 1272 (all), 1482 (all) and the 1252.03 search excerpt. Not read: 1274, the rest of Title Four (subdivision), Chapter 1488 (storm water), 1046 beyond its section title and the Ellwood City Borough Mobile Home Specifications. path.note: A second unit on a house lot is not a listed use, and 'Any use not expressly listed for a district is prohibited in that district', so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). A house may become a two-family dwelling by special exception in R-1 and by right in R-2 (see the other paths)

unlisted_use_path.note: 'A land use not expressly delineated as a permitted use, conditional use, or special exception maybe permitted as a conditional use' when its impacts are 'equal to or less than any use specifically listed in the Zoning District'. Borough Council decides after the Planning Commission's recommendation (1264.05, 1266.04). The C-3 Downtown lists name 'Compatible uses not otherwise listed'. 1266.04 bars any use not expressly listed, so outside C-3 this path is not read as open, though 1272.35's own words name no district. In R-1 and R-2 a second unit may be read as the listed two-family dwelling, not an unlisted use, and in the C-3 Gateway North overlay as the listed duplex (see the other paths)

unlisted_use_scope.note: The Borough weighs employees, floor area, products, walk-in trade and traffic, which fit a business better than a home
unlisted_use_scope.quote: A use which is not specifically listed in a particular zoning district, but which is determined by the Borough, in accordance with the express standards and criteria set forth in this chapter, to be similar in characteristics and impacts to another use which is specifically listed in the same zoning district

value.name: Multi-family dwelling - duplex (C-3 Gateway North)
value.conditions: A duplex by conditional use in the C-3 Gateway North overlay. Borough Council decides after the Planning Commission's review and a hearing, and may approve only if the use conforms to the district, conditional use and general regulations, fits its surroundings and has adequate off-street parking that does not back onto a street or alley (1264.05). Parking on the same lot and not in the front lawn, and a traffic impact study (1272.27). A residential lot 40 ft wide, front yard at least 10 ft and at most 20 ft on 5th Street (elsewhere 5 ft by the text, 10 ft by the table), side yards 10 ft, rear yard 20 ft, lot coverage 80%, height 50 ft. value.name: Multifamily dwelling above the ground floor (C-1, C-2)
value.conditions: Multifamily dwellings by conditional use in C-1 and C-2. The dwellings must be on floors above the ground floor, and their access may not be through a ground floor establishment (1272.23). Borough Council decides after the Planning Commission's review and a hearing, and may approve only if the use conforms to the district, conditional use and general regulations, fits its surroundings and has adequate off-street parking that does not back onto a street or alley (1264.05). No off-street parking is required in C-2 (1270.03(b))

requires.condition: Only for dwellings on floors above the ground floor, with access not through a ground floor establishment. A house lived in on its ground floor does not fit this as written

value.conditions: Multi-family dwellings by conditional use in the C-3 Gateway West and Institutional and Professional overlays. value.conditions: Residential uses on the second floor or above, not the ground floor, are permitted by right in the C-3 Core Commercial overlay

value.name: Apartments or townhouses (C-3 Gateway North)
value.conditions: Apartments and townhouses are permitted by right in the C-3 Gateway North overlay. An apartment building has three or more dwelling units, at least one above or below the others, and a townhouse building three to eight units side by side (1260.08(46), (47)). Two units in Gateway North are a duplex, a conditional use (see the duplex path)

value.name: Conversion of a nonconforming building to residential use
value.conditions: A nonconforming building or structure may be converted into residential uses by special exception. The Board must find it compatible with adjacent uses and buildings, without effect on the uses of nearby properties, not detrimental to public welfare and suited to the site, and it may attach reasonable conditions (1264.04). The district's yards and area apply, each living unit has at least 900 sq ft of habitable living area, so two units need at least 1,800 sq ft in all, one bathroom and three habitable rooms, and the Fire Chief certifies fire and safety

requires.condition: Only a nonconforming building or structure. A house is a nonconforming use in C-1, C-2 and the C-3 Core Commercial and Gateway West overlays, whose lists name no single-family dwelling, but whether converting a house that is already residential counts as a conversion into residential uses is not settled. A house that is nonconforming only by its yards or lot size must still meet the district's yards and area

value.note: A nonconforming use may not be extended or changed except to a conforming use (1268.01(b)). An addition to it is a special exception only if attached, within the district's yards and height, for the use that existed in 1997 and at most 80% of the building's fair market value then (1268.08)

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists an accessory dwelling unit. R-1 lists two-family dwellings by special exception and R-2 by right

value.condition: In the floodway any encroachment that would raise flood heights is prohibited, and 'No new construction or development shall be allowed, unless a permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office'. No expansion of an existing structure in the floodway may raise the base flood elevation, and no variance may be granted that would.

In the flood fringe and the general floodplain 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless a permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office'. It is read here for a new building or an addition.

In the identified floodplain new construction or a substantial improvement of a residential structure has its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft, and enclosed space below the lowest floor is prohibited. Fill reaches 15 ft beyond the building. Work of 50% or more of market value is a substantial improvement in full compliance. New construction is a structure begun on or after June 1, 1982, with its later improvements. In a flood fringe with no designated floodway no new development may raise the base flood elevation by more than one foot with all past and projected development. Manufactured homes and any addition to one are prohibited in the floodplain unless a variance is granted, and then they are on a permanent foundation, elevated 1 1/2 ft above the base flood elevation and anchored. All structures must be built to resist the 100-year flood. The Zoning Hearing Board hears floodplain variances (1264.02(a)(3), 1482.17).

C-3 Downtown overlay figures. Core Commercial (CC): lot width 30 ft, no front, side or rear yard, a front yard of at most 10 ft, lot coverage 100%, height 50 ft. Gateway West (GW): residential lot width 40 ft, no front yard, side yards 10 ft, rear yard 20 ft, a front yard of at most 20 ft, coverage 90%, height 50 ft. Gateway North (GN): residential lot 40 ft wide, front yard 10 ft, side yards 10 ft, rear yard 20 ft, coverage 80%, height 50 ft. Institutional and Professional (IP): residential lot 5,000 sq ft and 40 ft wide, front yard 10 ft, side yards 10 ft, rear yard 20 ft, coverage 85%, height 40 ft. The overlay table gives 5,000 sq ft of lot area per family in each overlay.
